papers.title: PDAcc: A Prefill-Decode Disaggregated MCM-Based Accelerator for Multi-Task Large Language Model Applications
papers.abstract: Prefill-decode (PD) disaggregation has emerged as a promising serving paradigm for large language models (LLMs), as it decouples prompt processing (prefill) from autoregressive token generation (decode) to reduce inter-task interference and improve quality of service (QoS). However, disaggregation also amplifies stage imbalance: the prefill cluster (P-C) can become compute-limited, the decode cluster (D-C) is often bandwidth-limited, and the required cross-device KV cache transfer introduces additional communication overhead. This work presentsPDAcc, a four-chiplet multi-chip-module (MCM) accelerator optimized for PD-disaggregated LLM inference. PDAcc employs reconfigurable chiplets that can be dynamically assigned to prefill or decode according to workload ratios. It further introduces three techniques: copy-less float hybrid-LUT multiply (CFHM) to repurpose idle on-chip SRAM for prefill acceleration, hybrid compressed weight gather (HCWG) to utilize prefill-side bandwidth and improve inter-chip weight delivery for decode, and cross-cluster attention dataflow (CCAD) to reduce dependency traffic by shifting part of attention computation across clusters. Implemented in 22-nm technology as a four-chiplet MCM, PDAcc sustains 541–4727 effective tokens/s on GPT-2, OPT, and Llama 3.2, achieving$5.76\times $higher prefill throughput and$12.42\times $higher decode throughput than a single chiplet, and further delivering an additional 1.50–$3.24\times $improvement over a four-chiplet PD-aggregated baseline with the same MCM scaling.
